A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {S, A, P, r, \gamma}$ be a [[Definition:Markov Decision Process|Markov decision process]] with [[Definition:Finite Set|finite]] state space and discount $\gamma \in \hointr 0 1$.
Then the [[Definition:Optimal Value Function|optimal value function]] $V^*$ is the [[Definition:Unique|unique]] solution of:
:$\displaystyle \map {V^*} s = \max_{a \mathop \in A} \paren {\map r {s, a} + \gamma \sum_{s' \mathop \in S} \map P {s' \mid s, a} \map {V^*} {s'} }$

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]].
Let $T: X \to X$ satisfy $\map d {T x, T y} \le q \, \map d {x, y}$ for some $q < 1$.
Then $T$ has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]], and $T^n x \to x^*$ for all $x \in X$.

substitutions.the complete metric space: the space of bounded value functions with the supremum norm

validity_conditions: the discount factor must be strictly less than one for the Bellman operator to contract
rewards must be bounded so the space of value functions is complete under the supremum norm
the maximum over actions must be attained, which holds for finite action sets
proof_plan:
Let $\map B S$ be the space of [[Definition:Bounded Mapping|bounded]] real functions on $S$ with the [[Definition:Supremum Norm|supremum norm]].
$\map B S$ is [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete]].

Define the [[Definition:Bellman Operator|Bellman optimality operator]]:
:$\displaystyle \map {\paren {\TT V} } s = \max_{a \mathop \in A} \paren {\map r {s, a} + \gamma \sum_{s'} \map P {s' \mid s, a} \map V {s'} }$
By the [[Banach Fixed-Point Theorem]], $\TT$ has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]] $V^*$.
